His servant, however, whose name was Buzabah, did not consent to come,
but went to the West
and ruled over Africa.
And in this year,
which is the year 1497
of the Greeks [1186 AD],
there was a conjunction of six wandering stars (planets) in the zodiacal sign of Libra,
except for Mars,
which was seen in Gemini on the fourteenth of Elul,
in the sixth month of the Arabs (Jumada II).
And all the astrologers predicted beforehand
that a universal deluge by a violent wind would occur in the world,
and destroy all human beings,
just as that which occurred in the days of Noah at the approach of the sign of Pisces,
and waters swept over the whole earth.
Now Qilij Arslan, the Sultan of Iconium, believed this fabrication more than anyone else,
and incurred great losses,
and made underground vaults in the earth,
and built strong houses in the depths.
God, however,
— praise to His grace! —
showed their prediction to be empty and vain.
And when that famous day arrived,
and many had fortified themselves in underground vaults and caves,
a clear and serene atmosphere appeared, with great calmness more than all other days,
and there was only an eclipse of the sun, as usual.
And the astrologers were held in contempt by kings and commoners {OCR?: nobles},
because of the falsehood of their art.
Now a certain man among the famous astrologers among them used to say
that they were lying in what they predicted.
And when the Sultan summoned him and asked him,
he said the very same thing,
and he even gave his signature
that nothing of what they said would happen,
nor would anything evil befall mankind.
And when his word came true,
the Sultan inquired of him,
"From where did you know this?" And he replied,
"I did not speak from the art [of astrology],
but I knew that if the deluge occurs,
neither will I remain,
nor those who would blame me;
and if it does not occur,
I will carry off the crown of victory,
just as I have carried it off!"
And the Sultan laughed,
and gave him a gift and dismissed him.
And at that time, the Prince, the lord of Antioch, made peace with Saladin,
and by deceit he seized Rupen, the ruler of Cilicia, weighed him down with irons, and imprisoned him.
And he gathered an army and entered Cilicia,
and Leon stood valiantly against him,
and the Prince returned in shame.
